A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same homomorphic spatial-embedding analysis and Latent Space Algebra benchmark. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original recursive-probing experiments on ViT, DINOv2, and ResNet representations across three transformation levels, including empirical loss trajectories in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original recursive-probing results, model-size comparisons, and atomic linearity experiments using linear regression and Orthogonal Procrustes Analysis, presented in Figure 3 and Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: v1 uses one shared linear probe applied to concatenated image and action embeddings. v2 replaces it with six independent generator-specific linear probes (Section 5.3 and Appendix B.1), allowing different state transformations for different generators. This substantially changes the diagnostic procedure’s expressivity, although frozen backbones and recursive application remain.

E1.justification: Two central benchmark levels change their transformation requirements. Level 2 replaces translation plus isotropic scaling with translation plus in-plane rotation. Level 3 replaces mixed rotation, scaling, and translation with six pure axis rotations at ±30 degrees (Appendix A). The seven Stanford object classes remain unchanged; Armadillo’s added illustration does not represent new object coverage.

E2.justification: The reference predictor defining structural failure changes from identity persistence, predicting the initial embedding, to the global mean of target features. v2 also introduces an evaluated comparison between orthogonal Procrustes fits and unrestricted affine regression in Table 4. These substantially revise the empirical controls; the original backbone families remain.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 50 epochs with batch size 1024 to 100 epochs with batch size 256. v2 expands three base backbones to nine size/depth variants and replaces MSE/cosine evaluation with MSE and mean-normalized Ratio Loss. The new atomic analysis specifies 3000 pairs per transformation and an 80/20 split. Atomic training and recursive evaluation through length 20 are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic model-size/depth comparisons and atomic linearity analyses comparing affine and orthogonal fits across translation distances and rotation axes/angles (Figure 3(c), Appendices C–D). These investigate capacity and probe-optimization explanations. Conversely, v1’s MSE-versus-cosine sensitivity analysis and associated supervised-invariance analysis are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 and report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional model variants and deterministic OPA comparisons do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main trajectories and quantitative findings are revised: the reported Level 3/Level 1 absolute-error gap changes from 3–3.8 times in v1 Figure 2 to 5.73–17.72 times in v2 Figure 3. Tables 2–4 add recursive, scaling, and atomic-fit results; for example, a 30-degree Y rotation has linear R2 of 0.3163 and OPA R2 of -0.0286. Changed tasks, probes, and normalization preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.1’s formal rendering-map construction and induced group-action derivation, revises the finite-group reduction in Lemma 4.3, and removes v1’s Abelian Collapse corollary. The input-projection and RoPE arguments also change their stated circuit bounds from NC0 to TC0. These are substantive mathematical revisions beyond reordered exposition.

C1.justification: The central conditional complexity barrier and the three principal contributions remain. v2 explicitly emphasizes single-forward-pass execution and narrows the introduction’s empirical contribution from failure on non-abelian dynamics generally to degradation on non-solvable dynamics. This refines the claim’s scope without replacing the central thesis.

C2.justification: v1 explains supervised-model failures through objective-induced invariance and divergent MSE/cosine behavior. v2 removes that account and emphasizes depth-scaling insensitivity and OPA as excluding capacity and optimization explanations. Its claim that orthogonal-fit failure establishes the absence of any valid linear operator is a substantial new interpretation that exceeds the restricted fitting test.

D1.justification: v2 documents revised probe and training configurations, parameter/layer counts for nine backbones, separate training/testing settings, and the atomic analysis’s sampling, 768-dimensional CLS features, and split. Some earlier details disappear, including explicit ViT ImageNet-21k pretraining and patch-size identifiers. Appendix B.1 also retains a 2d-to-d probe description without clearly identifying the second concatenated input, unlike v1’s explicit state/action formula.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Chen and Artzi, Curless and Levoy, Hall, Klein, Poincaré, and Thomas et al., and motivates group-based evaluation through the Erlangen Program. The main positioning against spatial-reasoning and circuit-complexity literature remains. Publication-year and venue updates to retained works do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, theoretical exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries gain substantial explanatory framing and place the word problem before circuit complexity; the architectural and task bounds are reorganized. Appendix A is restructured, and new quantitative and atomic-analysis appendices materially change the document’s organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned with an illustrative spatial-failure panel, Algorithm 1 disappears, and a new workflow Figure 2 explains recursive probing. The former multi-metric plots are replaced by a full-width composite Figure 3 covering errors, normalization, and scaling. v2 also redesigns the dataset illustration, expands Table 1’s structure, and adds three numerical result tables.

improvement.justification: Generator-specific probes remove v1’s shared state-matrix restriction, making the empirical test more appropriate, while cleaner transformation controls and explicit numerical tables improve assessability. The net gain is limited by overinterpretation of the new OPA evidence: orthogonal-fit failure does not exclude all linear maps, and Table 4 reports a positive 0.0168 for a 30-degree X rotation despite claiming consistently negative out-of-plane scores. The revised theory also leaves the central inference from encoding a final image to solving its transformation word insufficiently established.
